title: Cross-team commitment protocols for canary experiments (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working protocol to align product, serving/runtime, SRE, and CS on the minimal set of commitments required to run safe, scalable canaries and A/B tests for console-driven rollout features. Focus is on creating a predictable choreography: who does what at each stage, when to abort, and what artifacts are non-negotiable before traffic moves.

Why this doc exists (pain we saw):
- Past canaries stalled because teams disagreed on success criteria mid-experiment.
- Ops time spent debugging regressions that were actually expected behavior because experiment metadata was missing.
- Slow emergency responses due to unclear on-call responsibilities across product/infra.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to staged feature rollouts and model/route swaps performed via Console rollouts or feature flags.
- Not intended for infra-only maintenance (kernel upgrades, infra patches) unless those affect routing or model binaries.
- Assumes telemetry hooks are available per-route and conversation-level IDs are present in logs.

High-level commitments (one-liners):
- Product: owns the experiment hypothesis, success metric, alarm thresholds, and customer-facing comms.
- Serving/runtime: owns rollout configuration, fallback chains, and capacity throttles.
- SRE: owns platform-level SLO alarms, rollback automation, and escalation path.
- CS/Success: owns customer watchlist and coordinates targeted notifications if customers are in the canary cohort.
- Metrics/observability: ensures dashboards and derivative metrics (quality deltas) are live before traffic shifts.

Pre-launch checklist (all must be green before enclave traffic):
1) Hypothesis + Acceptance: product doc link + primary metric + minimum detectable effect (MDE) and evaluation window.
2) Rollout Plan: slice definitions, cohort assignment method (cookie, id hashing), percent schedule, and fallback model ids.
3) Telemetry Contract: list of required metrics (per-route token cost, P50/P95 latency, server errors 5xx, user-facing error types, eval-quality score) and log identifiers.
4) Dashboards: live panels for primary metric, guardrail metrics and cost, with 5-min refresh.
5) Alerts: preconfigured alert rules with on-call targets (pager duty services) and clear severity.
6) Runbook Stub: short emergency rollback steps (console toggle, service rollback, infra reroute).
7) Stakeholders Notified: rotation calendar entry, Slack channel, dedicated thread, handbook page update.
8) Canary Tickets: Jira ticket with experiment parameters + rollout artifact links.

Commitment matrix (who does what):
- Product (owner): finalize hypothesis, tag experiment in DB, write acceptance criteria, prepare comms.
- Serving/runtime: prepare model variants, verify compatibility, stage rollout JSON, provide expected throughput envelope.
- SRE: configure pagers, confirm canary slice isolation, review autoscaler thresholds.
- Observability: wire synthetic checks, smoke tests, and quality-eval jobs.
- CS/Legal (if needed): sign off customer notifications + data retention notes.

Decision gates and timeboxes:
- Warmup: 0–10% traffic for 30–60 minutes to catch immediate regressions.
- Stability gate: maintain guardrail thresholds for at least 2 window periods (default 2 hours) before moving to next slice.
- Increment cadence: double or +10% (choose smaller) depending on capacity risk.
- Maximum canary duration: 72 hours unless stakeholder review extends.

Abort criteria (explicit):
- Latency: P95 increase > 2x baseline or P50 > 300ms above baseline for 30m.
- Errors: global 5xx rate spike > 3x baseline sustained for 10m.
- Quality: automated eval delta below minimum acceptable threshold (MDE) for experiment.
- Cost: per-token cost jump > 30% without comms or expected reason.
- Security/PII: any surfaced customer data leakage or unauthorized access.

Abort actions (fast):
1) Product issues abort command + message in channel.
2) Serving/runtime triggers immediate routing to fallback model id.
3) SRE escalates to on-call and optionally reverts infra change.
4) CS drafts customer-facing note if customers affected.

Communication choreography (templates):
- Pre-launch Slack: short blurb with hypothesis, percent, timers, dashboards, and who to call.
- Abort message: reason, time window, traffic % affected, and immediate mitigation steps.
- Post-mortem invite: link to retrospective doc + stakeholders.
(Templates appended as quick pastable snippets in the console copy library.)

Experiment metadata taxonomy (required tags on every canary ticket):
- experiment_id (console-assigned), product_area, model_family, rollout_strategy, cohort_key, start_time_utc, expected_end_time_utc, MDE_primary_metric, rollback_trigger.

Telemetry contract (minimal metric set):
- primary.metric.value (string or numeric)
- primary.metric.delta (relative to baseline)
- route.latency.p50/p95 (ms)
- route.errors.4xx, route.errors.5xx (counts and rates)
- cost.per_token (USD)
- quality.eval.score (same eval harness used in preflight)
- user-visible-failure.rate
- synthetic.smoke.passing (bool)

Quick SLO-aware slicing heuristic (ops-friendly):
- Avoid putting high-SLA customers in first 10% unless feature is opt-in.
- Prefer hashed-id slices that map evenly across regions and tenants.
- Exclude VIP tenant IDs from random cohorts unless a deliberate targeted test.

Rollout automation knobs (operational rules):
- Auto-halt on any severity pager firing.
- Auto-revert if P95 latency doubled in 10 minutes.
- Allow manual override by product + SRE after 1-hour coordinated review.

Post-release checks (0–24h):
- Validate telemetry ingestion for all required metrics.
- Confirm synthetic checks across regions.
- Run quality evaluation against sample prompt set.
- Snapshot cost report for the canary slice.

Postmortem structure (if abort or unexpected regression):
- Timeline of events (timestamps)
- Root cause hypothesis + evidence
- Who executed which action
- Corrective steps and follow-up owners
- Customer notification log (if applicable)

Low-friction experiments (mini-canary variant):
- Use 1–2% traffic, shorter windows (15–30m), only for UI surface changes or telemetry-only experiments.
- Require fewer signoffs (product + obs) but still need rollback automation and alerts.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we automatically annotate traces with experiment_id at the proxy layer? (ops + infra)
- What is the canonical place to store the MDE calculation and power analysis? (product analytics)
- How do we encode multi-model experiments (fallback chains) in the console UI without confusing SLO logic? (design + serving)
- Draft a lightweight API contract for the telemetry team to validate metric schemas pre-launch.

Notes to self / friction points we've hit before:
- Teams often forget to whitelist canary dashboards for external auditors—add to preflight.
- When rollback isn't immediate, stale KV caches can continue serving bad outputs; add a cache-invalidation bullet to runbook.
- Cost alarms have been noisy; separate cost-warning vs cost-critical thresholds.

Next steps (practical):
1) Walk this doc with 15-minute cross-functional sync next Tuesday.
2) Bake experiment_id enforcement into console UI (design ticket).
3) Add rollout templates for small/medium/large risk profiles.
4) Ship a sample Slack template library into shared console resources.

Appendix (short snippets):
- Slack pre-launch: "LAUNCH: canary gen2 v3 -> 5% at 2025-03-10T14:00Z. Hypothesis: reduce halluc rate by 12% w/o latency increase. Dashboard: <link>. On-call: #sre-oncall, PD: svc-obs. Abort: any P95 > +250ms or quality delta < -8%"
- Abort quick command: "/canary abort <experiment_id>" (console will route to fallback)

If you want to be ruthless about minimizing blast radius, we should default to conservative slices and make the friction for bigger slices explicit rather than implicit.

-- Maya
